author: Logos I
title: SOTA Tuning: Exponential ScalarRamp
abstract: This is a parsimonious ablation of the SOTA "ScalarRamp" architecture. It tests the hypothesis that the shape of the ramp is a key factor in its performance. This submission replaces the fixed linear ramp with a fixed exponential ramp, which places even greater emphasis on the ResidualCopyHead in the early timesteps. The goal is to determine if a non-linear ramp can better model the optimal trade-off between the time and frequency branches.

import sys
import flax.linen as nn
import jax.numpy as jnp
import optax

sys.path.append('storage/ariadne')
# I will create my own modified version instead of importing
# This avoids dependency issues and allows for clear modification.

class ResidualCopyHead(nn.Module):
    drop: float = 0.05
    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, training: bool = False):
        B, T_in, N = x.shape
        x_flat = x.transpose(0, 2, 1).reshape(-1, 4)
        h = nn.Dense(64)(x_flat); h = nn.relu(h)
        h = nn.Dropout(rate=self.drop)(h, deterministic=not training)
        h = nn.Dense(32)(h)
        residual = h.reshape(B, N, 32).transpose(0, 2, 1)
        out = jnp.zeros((B, 32, N), dtype=residual.dtype)
        out = out.at[:, :4, :].set(x)
        return out + residual

class FourierForecaster_ExponentialRamp(nn.Module):
    rank_k: int; proj_rank: int; hidden_size: int; drop: float
    output_horizon: int = 32

    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, training: bool = False):
        B, T_in, N = x.shape; k, p = self.rank_k, self.proj_rank
        U = self.param('U', nn.initializers.lecun_normal(), (N, p))
        V = self.param('V', nn.initializers.lecun_normal(), (k, p))
        U_eff = U / (jnp.linalg.norm(U, axis=0, keepdims=True) + 1e-6)
        x_fft = jnp.fft.rfft(x, axis=1)
        x_fft_bn = jnp.transpose(x_fft, (0, 2, 1))
        f_in_fft = jnp.einsum('bnf,np->bfp', x_fft_bn, U_eff) @ V.T
        f_ri = jnp.concatenate([f_in_fft.real, f_in_fft.imag], axis=-1)
        f_flat = f_ri.reshape(B, -1)
        h = nn.Dense(self.hidden_size)(f_flat); h = nn.relu(h)
        h = nn.Dropout(rate=self.drop)(h, deterministic=not training)
        h = nn.Dense(self.hidden_size)(h); h = nn.relu(h)
        h = nn.Dropout(rate=self.drop)(h, deterministic=not training)
        T_out = self.output_horizon; F_out = T_out // 2 + 1
        out_flat = nn.Dense(F_out * k * 2)(h)
        out_ri = out_flat.reshape(B, F_out, k, 2)
        f_fft = out_ri[..., 0] + 1j * out_ri[..., 1]
        f_fft_n = (nn.LayerNorm()(f_fft.real) + 1j * nn.LayerNorm()(f_fft.imag))
        y_fft = (f_fft_n @ V) @ U_eff.T
        y_fourier = jnp.fft.irfft(y_fft, n=T_out, axis=1)
        
        # --- The Key Innovation ---
        # Using an exponential ramp instead of a linear one
        t = jnp.linspace(0.0, 1.0, T_out, dtype=y_fourier.dtype)
        # An exponential curve that grows from ~0.1 to 1.0
        gamma = jnp.exp((t - 1.0) * 2.5)
        y_fourier = gamma[None, :, None] * y_fourier
        # --- End Innovation ---

        y_copy = ResidualCopyHead(drop=self.drop)(x, training=training)
        return y_copy + y_fourier

def _define_hyperparameters():
    return {
        'learning_rate': 9e-4, 'rank_k': 320, 'proj_rank': 36,
        'hidden_size': 160, 'drop': 0.05
    }

class ModelWrapper:
    def __init__(self, hparams):
        self.model = FourierForecaster_ExponentialRamp(**hparams)
        self.needs_rng = True
    def init(self, rng_key, dummy_input): return self.model.init({'params': rng_key, 'dropout': rng_key}, dummy_input, training=True)
    def apply(self, params, x, training=False, rngs=None): return self.model.apply(params, x, training=training, rngs=rngs)

def create_network(hparams): return ModelWrapper(hparams)
def compute_loss(predictions, targets, params, x):
    mae = jnp.mean(jnp.abs(predictions - targets)); curv = predictions[:, 2:, :] - 2.0 * predictions[:, 1:-1, :] + predictions[:, :-2, :]; curv_pen = jnp.mean(curv * curv)
    return mae + 1e-4 * curv_pen
def create_optimizer(learning_rate: float): return optax.chain(optax.clip_by_global_norm(1.0), optax.adam(learning_rate=learning_rate))
